mean: (of effects or feelings) to linger on
lit: to drag a tail behind: something has passed, but its tail is still trailing after it

near.diff: 後を引く also lingers, but is used above all for food or habits you can't stop at one of; 尾を引く is for after-effects of an event.

bad.en: (meant: he took the dog out for a walk on its lead)

lit: knocked down by its own looks: it looks impressive, but falls short of what the looks promise

mean: (of experience or money) to be what counts

mean: that saves a lot of explaining

near.diff: 話が違う protests that things are not as agreed; 話が早い welcomes that things can move quickly without explanation.

mean: to be deeply grateful for a favour

mean: to work at something without a break

near.diff: 身を粉にする is wearing oneself out labouring, often for others; 寝る間も惜しむ stresses cutting sleep to make time.

ctx.s: 彼女[かのじょ]は{寝[ね]る間[ま]も惜[お]しんで}ピアノの練習[れんしゅう]を続[つづ]けた。
ctx.en: She kept practising the piano, grudging even the hours she spent asleep.

ctx.s: 「あの頃[ころ]は{寝[ね]る間[ま]も惜[お]しんで}、毎晩[まいばん]明[あ]け方[がた]まで働[はたら]いたなあ。」
ctx.en: "Back then I grudged myself sleep and worked until dawn every night."

ctx.s: 創業者[そうぎょうしゃ]は{寝[ね]る間[ま]も惜[お]しんで}製品[せいひん]の開発[かいはつ]に打[う]ち込[こ]んだという。
ctx.en: The founder is said to have thrown himself into developing the product, giving up sleep to do it.

ctx.s: 面白[おもしろ]い小説[しょうせつ]に夢中[むちゅう]になり、{寝[ね]る間[ま]も惜[お]しんで}読[よ]んだ。
ctx.en: I was so absorbed in the gripping novel that I read it at the expense of sleep.

ctx.s: {寝[ね]る間[ま]も惜[お]しむ}ほどの努力[どりょく]があったからこそ、今[いま]の成功[せいこう]がある。
ctx.en: It's precisely because of effort so intense he begrudged himself sleep that he is successful now.

bad.s: 心配[しんぱい]で、昨夜[さくや]は{寝[ね]る間[ま]も惜[お]しんだ}。
bad.en: (meant: I was so worried I couldn't sleep last night)
bad.why: It is choosing to give up sleep for something you are devoted to, not insomnia. For worry, say shinpai de nemurenakatta.

bad.s: {寝[ね]る間[ま]も惜[お]しんで}、五分[ごふん]でメールを一通[いっつう]書[か]いた。
bad.en: (meant: I worked hard and wrote one email in five minutes)
bad.why: It describes sustained effort over nights, days or weeks. A five-minute task cannot cost you any sleep.
